name: Lightning Process (LP)
founders: Phil Parker (UK osteopath, NLP practitioner/coach; self-described PhD in psychology of health)
founded_year_range: 1999 (site FAQ: 'created in 1999 by Dr Phil Parker'; Wikipedia: late 1990s)
delivery: trainer-led seminar (3 days, ~12 h total, group or 1:1, in person or online)
cost_summary: UK average about GBP 900 for the 3-day course plus follow-up sessions (~GBP 50/h; FAQ 2026). Prices vary by country and practitioner. About NOK 21,000 in Norway (no.wikipedia). Practitioners are licensed and pass part of their fees to the trademark holder.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
mechanism_summary: A chronically activated 'Physical Emergency Response' (fight-or-flight) produces allostatic load that impairs sleep, immunity, healing and energy. Habitual neural pathways of arousal, attention, thought and language keep the loop going. Repeated practice of a proprietary interrupt technique is meant to rewire these pathways through neuroplasticity. The site calls ME/CFS a physical illness and LP 'neuro-physiological', not psychological. The same model is applied to every condition.
techniques: Part 1 audio (~4 h) on the PER and neuroplasticity rationale, plus a readiness commitment
3-day seminar (~12 h total) in a small group or 1:1
Recognising activation of the Physical Emergency Response
Proprietary physical-and-verbal interrupt routine (movement, posture, gestures, spoken phrases) repeated many times daily
Self-coaching and goal-setting; return to activity
mainstream_notes: Not available on the NHS. NICE NG206 (2021), rec. 1.12.27 (verified): 'Do not offer the Lightning Process, or therapies based on it, to people with ME/CFS.' The SMILE paediatric RCT ran in an NHS specialist service (Bath/Bristol) but did not lead to adoption. The UK ASA upheld 2 of 4 challenges to the website's claims after a 2011 Hampshire Trading Standards referral. The World ME Alliance (2022) and the UK and Norwegian ME associations oppose it. In Norway, NAV has sometimes recommended and part-funded courses. Recovery Norge (Henrik Vogt; network 2017, organisation 2018; LP instructor Live Landmark among the founders) gave user input to an NTNU trial of an LP-derived 3-day intervention. That trial's ethics approval was revoked in 2021 over a COI and restored in 2022. A McMaster University long COVID RCT of LP vs pacing (FALCON, NCT07697261) was seeking ethics approval in 2026 amid a petition to pause it.
insurance_notes: Self-pay only. No insurer or CMS coverage. Occasional ad hoc welfare or municipal funding (NAV and municipalities in Norway).

key_trials.citation: Crawley EM, Gaunt DM, Garfield K, et al. Clinical and cost-effectiveness of the Lightning Process in addition to specialist medical care for paediatric chronic fatigue syndrome: randomised controlled trial (SMILE). Arch Dis Child 2018;103(2):155-164; correction and editor's note 2019;104(10):e3-e4
key_trials.design: Pragmatic open-label RCT, SMC vs SMC+LP, ages 12-18, mild/moderate CFS/ME
key_trials.finding: SF-36 PF favoured LP by +12.5 (95% CI 4.5-20.5) at 6 mo and +15.1 (5.8-24.4) at 12 mo. Fatigue and anxiety improved at 6 mo; depression and school attendance also improved at 12 mo. Only 81 were analysed at 6 mo. The 2019 correction acknowledged retrospective registration, outcome switching and inclusion of feasibility-phase participants.

key_trials.citation: Reme SE, Archer N, Chalder T. Experiences of young people who have undergone the Lightning Process to treat CFS/ME: a qualitative study. Br J Health Psychol 2013;18(3):508-525
key_trials.finding: 7/9 much improved, 2 not. Criticisms included secrecy, intensity, little follow-up and feeling blamed when it failed.

key_trials.citation: Fauske L, Bruland OS, Dahl AA, Myklebostad A, Reme SE. Does the Lightning Process training programme reduce chronic fatigue in AYA cancer survivors? A mixed-methods pilot study. Cancers 2021;13(16):4076
key_trials.finding: Total fatigue score fell from baseline at 3 and 6 months (p<0.001). The authors call for a controlled study.

key_trials.citation: Parker P, Aston J, de Rijk L. A systematic review of the evidence base for the Lightning Process. Explore (NY) 2021;17(4):372-379
key_trials.finding: 14 studies, mostly uncontrolled. Evidence called 'emerging'; no meta-analysis.

key_trials.citation: Arroll B, Moir F, Jenkins E, Menkes DB. An audit of 12 cases of long COVID following the Lightning Process intervention examining benefits and harms. J Family Med Prim Care 2025;14(2):796-799 (erratum 2025;14:4407; critical letter Steinkopf 2025;14:5237-8)
key_trials.finding: 11/12 reported being ≥85% back to normal; no harms reported.

key_trials.citation: Finch F, Parker P, Nollett C, Burns S. The novel application of the Lightning Process to treat long COVID in primary care: case report. Explore (NY) 2024;20(2):248-252
Kielland A, Liu J, Jason LA. Do diagnostic criteria for ME matter to patient experience with services and interventions? J Health Psychol 2023;28(13):1189-1203
key_trials.design: Independent online survey using respondent-driven sampling (LP among the interventions rated)
key_trials.finding: On average, patients rated most interventions as having low-to-negative effects. Higher PEM was strongly associated with worse experience of interventions.

controversy: The SMILE trial was corrected in 2019 for retrospective registration, outcome switching and inclusion of feasibility-phase participants; critics such as David Tuller wanted it retracted. The ASA upheld 2 of 4 challenges (ruling c. 2012), and NICE 2021 recommends against LP. The Norwegian ME Association member survey (~2012-13, n=1,096 respondents) found 49% of LP course-takers worse vs 21% better, and a 2015 NAFKAM report found 39% had a negative course. Participants report secrecy rules and being blamed when it fails. In November 2011 NRK reported a 13-year-old's breakdown and suicide attempt after a course. In the BMJ (Hawkes, 2017) it was called secretive with a 'cultish quality'. In BBC File on 4 (2024), a coach told the reporter there was 'nothing physical wrong'. Neuroscientist Camilla Nord criticised its neuroscience framing. Other criticisms: a trademark fee-sharing model likened to MLM, and conflicts of interest in research (founder-authored reviews; Norwegian ethics reversal in 2021). The 2026 McMaster FALCON trial drew a petition with more than 1,700 signatures. The site's claims of '0 side effects' and of 17 or 18 peer-reviewed studies (the number is inconsistent) overstate the evidence.

popularity.reach_estimate: ~75,000-100,000 people cumulatively. Based on the founder's claim of >75,000 clients since 1999 (unverified); plausible given a long-standing licensed practitioner network in the UK, Norway and elsewhere.
popularity.method_notes: Trajectory is anchored on documented events. 2007-2012: UK media and survey peak; Norwegian uptake; 2009 Landmark memoir; 2010 book; ASA ruling; NRK coverage (Nov 2011). 2013: SMILE feasibility papers. 2017-2018: SMILE results and BMJ coverage; Recovery Norge founded. 2021: NICE recommendation against. 2022-2025: long COVID case reports and audit. 2024: BBC File on 4. 2026: McMaster FALCON trial controversy. Reach rests on the founder's >75k claim (unverified). The web-search budget was exhausted, so Google Trends and Reddit metrics were not retrieved; levels are qualitative judgements from event density.
